claims.text: 3 Avenue & 60 Street had 65 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 12 pedestrians injured, 3 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $4.5 million a year.
44% of crashes here had only people in vehicles hurt, against 24% at the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: only people in vehicles hurt and a vehicle was going straight ahead in 38% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 20% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading south in 33% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 17% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 2.0 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $668,000 a year.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 1.0 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $347,000 a year; check on site: the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 is responsible for BKLYN/QUEENS EXP (I 278), Gowanus Expressway (I 278) (owner recorded in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory).
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for 3 Avenue, 60 Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 38, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 7.
A request letter to the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 and the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
